scope: Focused continuation of the pinned ECC scan: selected delivery-oriented skills (TDD, verification, E2E, change impact, documentation governance, AI regression, agentic workflow, self-evaluation), their directly linked local references/scripts and TDD helper dependency closure, selected agent definitions, and the available .agents skill projections/metadata. This is not a full catalog, agent-adapter, hook-runtime, or dependency-license review.

limits: Recursive Git tree was complete (6,674 entries; not truncated), with no submodule or symlink entries; 46 binary-named assets were indexed but not fetched.

Deep review remains representative: the source has 327 canonical skill entries, 72 agents, 98 legacy commands, and many platform-specific mirrors/adapters. This continuation read all ten eval-harness test suites, their shared helpers, package smoke test, test runner, CLI and directly linked schema/package helpers.

No upstream tests, CLI, package build, example, or candidate code was executed. In particular, cli.test.js directly imports and calls the candidate fixture; replay/security tests spawn Node processes with upstream preload/CLI code; package smoke test invokes npm pack/tar and the packaged example; these are outside the user-authorized read-only boundary.

The eval gate still unconditionally refuses candidate execution. Static checks, tests-as-written, replay fixtures, receipts, and held-out labels are not a completed evaluation, score, or proof of OS containment.

The eval-harness implementation, tests, schemas, and examples are under the root ECC MIT notice (LICENSE); package metadata identifies root package MIT. Eval core and tests use Node built-ins/local modules; package-lock has 304 package records, 301 with SPDX license identifiers and three without (entities, mdurl, punycode.js). Third-party license texts were not fetched/reviewed.

The package smoke test explicitly uses npm pack --ignore-scripts --offline and tar; package.json prepack runs build:opencode, which deletes .opencode/dist and invokes the local TypeScript compiler. This path was inspected only and not run. No dependency was installed.
Root ECC materials are MIT; a separate nested MIT notice for context-and-decisions names Matt Pocock. Other nested notices and third-party obligations are not fully assessed.
No external link was followed. Credential-related evidence records environment-variable names only, never values; no source code was executed or enabled.

This continuation statically inspected the selected delivery workflows and their direct support paths; it did not survey all 327 canonical skills, 72 agents, 98 commands, or all host projections. No source code, tests, hooks, validators, helper scripts, or package commands were executed.

Root LICENSE remains the applicable MIT notice for the selected materials; selected .agents skill copies and documentation support files were compared by exact tree blob identity. No additional nested notice was found in the selected paths. Third-party package/license obligations elsewhere in the source remain unresolved.

Read-only documentation audit helpers use Python standard library plus local git; package-manager detection depends on Node and local helper modules and may spawn which/where. Hook-validator integration was not deeply reviewed; its imports identify Ajv, jsonc-parser, and local hooks configuration dependencies. E2E examples require project-specific Playwright/browser setup.
The self-evaluation evaluator is a keyword/structure heuristic, not a calibrated semantic judge or benchmark score. No evaluator tests or empirical reliability study were reviewed.
Revision 6 corrects revision 5 inventory: three .agents projection paths that were checked and found absent are recorded as a coverage finding, not as source files.
